Package com.egradx.notification.channel.webhook

Class EgradxWebhookChannel

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.notification.channel.webhook.EgradxWebhookChannel
All Implemented Interfaces:
EgradxNotificationChannel
public class EgradxWebhookChannel extends Object implements EgradxNotificationChannel
Delivers a message as an HTTP POST of JSON to a URL — the address — for systems that are not a person: another application, an automation, a chat tool's incoming webhook. 

 POST <address>
 Content-Type: application/json
 Idempotency-Key: <deliveryId>          stable across retries of the same delivery
 X-Egradx-Delivery-Id: <deliveryId>
 X-Egradx-Timestamp: <unix seconds>
 X-Egradx-Signature: sha256=<hex>       when a signing secret is configured

 {"deliveryId": "…", "messageId": "…", "organizationId": "…", "notificationKey": "…",
  "subject": "…", "body": "…", "format": "TEXT", "attempt": 1}

Signing. With a secret in the organization's (or the all-organizations) webhook configuration, the signature is HMAC-SHA256 over "<timestamp>.<body>" with that secret. A receiver recomputes it to know the call came from here and was not altered, and rejects stale timestamps to stop replays. No configuration is needed otherwise: unlike email or Slack, a webhook has no provider account.

Failures. A 2xx is delivered. 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retryable, as is failing to connect. Any other 4xx is permanent — the receiver has said the request itself is wrong.

HTTPS only, unless egradx.notification.channels.webhook.allow-http is set for local development. Timeouts: 5 s to connect, 15 s for the whole call by default.
